EE – Curriculum

The EE curriculum enables students to design a customised programme comprising a specific set of courses, tailored to meet their individual interests and career goals. Design is emphasized in the curriculum through various project courses. In the first stage of the programme, students will receive broad-based training which, in addition to establishing a strong foundation in mathematics and computing, will also be immediately exposed to the use of electrical components and equipment in solving fundamental engineering problems in EE. They will also be introduced to the different areas in EE which are driving the technological developments of today. In the second stage, students will enrol in core courses that focus on fundamental knowledge in EE. These core courses provide the essential foundation for a variety of specialised technical areas in EE.

During their senior years of study, students may specialise in certain fields of EE through their selection of elective courses. Students can choose elective courses from a number of areas of concentrations as follows: Communications & Networks, Integrated Circuits & Embedded Systems, Control, Intelligent Systems & Robotics, Signal Analysis & Machine Intelligence, Microelectronics Technologies & Devices, Microwave and RF, and Power & Energy Systems. The elective courses in each concentration are categorized as extended-core and depth technical elective courses. An extended-core course enables students to achieve a broad understanding of concepts in the particular concentration. A depth technical elective is a higher-level course that provides greater depth and coverage in the particular concentration.

The extended-core courses are organised into concentration areas for students to achieve exposure to various facets of EE. To achieve depth, students need to read EE depth electives. By specific choice of electives, EE students will be able to specialise in a variety of areas. Click here for the Specialisations available to EE students. Students may take additional EE elective courses to satisfy the Unrestricted Electives (UE) requirement.
